in_latin.name: Jophaniel

in_latin.long_meaning: Jophaniel, a compound name derived from Jehovah (YHWH) and angelos (messenger), signifying God's salvation through messengers or angels, has its roots in Hebrew and Greek etymology. In the Bible, angels often served as messengers of God, playing a crucial role in the lives of the faithful. This name holds spiritual significance, emphasizing God's intervention and protection through divine messengers. Historically, this name has been used in Christian tradition to signify the divine presence and guidance in times of need.

in_english.name: Jophaniel
in_english.meaning: Name of God, Yahweh is salvation through messengers
in_english.long_meaning: Jophaniel, a name that combines the Hebrew Jehovah (YHWH) meaning God and the Greek angelos meaning messenger, is deeply rooted in the biblical concept of angels as divine messengers. In the New Testament, angels play a crucial role in the lives of the faithful, serving as harbingers of God's plan and agents of His salvation. This name holds significant spiritual meaning, as it highlights God's power and intervention through divine messengers. Historically, Jophaniel has been used in Christian tradition to signify God's presence and guidance in times of need, emphasizing the importance of trust and obedience in the face of adversity. As a given name, Jophaniel is often associated with qualities such as faith, hope, and perseverance, reflecting the characteristics of those who have trusted in God's plan and been saved through His messengers.
